column6: etymology
Older 朙 shows moon 月 shining through a window/opening 囧 → bright; later 囧 became sun 日, giving modern 日 + 月 → 明 “bright, clear.”
A person 大 wearing an ornate sheep-like headdress 羊 → beautiful, splendid.
Sun/light 日 gives the meaning “dim/dark”; 音 yīn (“sound,” anciently speech/voice coming from the mouth) gives the sound → dark, obscure, hidden.
An ancient building-like graph related to 高 “high,” probably suggesting an open/elevated structure filled with light → bright; exact pictorial origin uncertain.
Originally 醜 chǒu: ghost/demon 鬼 guǐ gives “repulsive, ugly”; 酉 yǒu “wine vessel” gives the sound → “ugly, shameful”; simplified to the unrelated 丑, originally a pictograph of a hand/claws.
